 Report `coverage.version:1` preserves known missing/truncated hours, visitor uncertainty, hours whose persisted ring progress was not advanced, and each built hour's horizon (including zero or unknown). Unadvanced progress does not mean every displayed credit is wrong. `minHorizonMs` is null when contributing horizons or sources are missing/unknown; legacy `hours.horizonMs` describes the old last-hour value, never a minimum. Stored legacy or malformed metadata cannot establish coverage; known warnings survive read-time normalization without rewriting reports. Both operator views show these limits before empty results. Maturity is always `unknown`, and status is only `incomplete` or `unknown`: neither age nor an empty warning list establishes delivery completeness, compatible policies or experimental readiness. Direct ledger reports cannot establish carry-in history. This bounded JSON/view contract does not change CSV exports, repair history or certify external consumers.
 
-New raw reports and hour aggregates record bounded `computation.version:1`: effective attribution policies/windows, per-slot reward/objective/decay tau, raw-day versus hourly-ring horizon/cap profile and the unweighted credited-outcome/item-decision unit. Carry-in-only credited slots are included even where the old arm projection has no denominator row. Day construction refuses unknown/mixed hourly bases or changed accumulator configuration before canonical replacement; estimator-only changes remain possible. Legacy saved days remain readable with unknown computation. Ambiguous duplicate-label custom reports preserve their existing response-only counts/grids but carry unknown computation. Valid basis survives full/paged diagnostics and the same-object summary. Windows expose per-slot `compatibility` status/reasons/dates and return no pooled arms for unknown, mixed or unrepresented contributions; this is withholding, not a zero result. The modern view shows these warnings. Equality establishes only recorded computation, not common served control/allocation/enrollment, metric/target versions, monetary outcomes or experimental compatibility. Objective/tau describe grids; arm credits remain unweighted repeated counts. There is no historical restamping/rebuild or policy choice. Older strict summary readers may reject the additive field; reader-first rollout requires separate qualification. Existing coverage, maturity, storage budgets and publication/history limitations remain.

The modern view shows these warnings. Existing coverage, maturity, storage budgets and publication/history limitations remain. Version3 identifies current-input logical deduplication after version2 exact-reference attribution. Stored versions1/2 keep their labels and counts; mixed versions cannot be pooled.
 
-Raw reports admit at most50,000 decisions and50,000 outcomes,6 policies including learning (the existing4 presets plus1 custom fit),800 raw ledger objects,16MiB per object and combined raw UTF-8 text,1,000,000 estimated work units,16,384 projected item/slot/ancestor cells across policies, and8MiB final report JSON. Work includes ring construction/sorting, policy/outcome filtering/sorting and featured-product cross-products; listing traversal is also bounded. Consumed components are limited to256 UTF-8 bytes and generated keys to2048 bytes; invalid shapes or inherited object-property names return400. Capacity refusal returns no-store413 with `code:report_budget_exceeded`, `budget`, `limit` and `observed`, before any partial raw publication; object refusals retain `objects`/`max`. General capped loader callers retain their separate truncation contract. Native object size and actual stream bytes are checked; text-only adapters can check actual bytes only after materialization. These are application safety budgets, not proved Worker CPU/memory, supported customer traffic or scientific policy limits.
+Raw/hourly readers compare complete logical records by tenant, stream and primary ID before distinct-row and ring caps. Exact decisions and validated nonce-bearing outcome retries count once; a changed payload or repeated nonce-free outcome ID refuses the report. Unique legacy outcomes remain supported. Only validated top-level `_ledger_delivery` transport provenance is excluded from equality. Optional `counts.duplicates:{decisions,outcomes}` records admitted repeats for the requested brand after erasure filtering and survives saved summaries; absence in an old report is unknown. This does not establish unique business orders or page views, online statistics idempotency, or complete delivery. Relevant ambiguous compact carry-in, including a forward input overlapping retained identity, refuses without repairing history; an already-folded-hour replay remains supported. Raw-input refusal precedes shard writes, but a later retained-shard failure can follow earlier shard progress, with no new hour aggregate published. Hourly full-record comparison now refuses above16MiB per object/combined physical UTF-8 text or1,000,000 admission work units. Retained-ID comparison across shards also has16MiB UTF-8 ID bytes and1,000,000 visited entries per build, with2048 bytes per relevant ID, checked before ring-cap projection. Physical object/byte/work caps still count duplicate traffic; these conservative application limits are not a supported customer envelope or deployed capacity proof.
 
+Raw reports admit at most50,000 distinct decisions and50,000 distinct outcomes,6 policies including learning (the existing4 presets plus1 custom fit),800 raw ledger objects,16MiB per object and combined raw UTF-8 text,1,000,000 estimated work units,16,384 projected item/slot/ancestor cells across policies, and8MiB final report JSON. These are application safety budgets, not proved Worker CPU/memory, supported customer traffic or scientific policy limits.
+
 Aggregate-to-day construction separately admits at most24 distinct canonical hours,16MiB combined aggregate JSON,6 policy names,1,000,000 estimated merge/admission work units,16,384 projected cells and8MiB report JSON before publication. Saved day reads admit8MiB per object; windows admit16MiB combined input and16,384 consumed/pooled rows or cells. Day/window GET responses are capped at8MiB including their response envelope. Required owner/shape failures and unavailable storage return sanitized no-store503; only an actual absent object is missing. These guards preserve accepted counts and conservative legacy coverage without rewriting stored objects. Legacy fallbacks or cardinality can refuse even below184 days; the date cap is not a native capacity guarantee. Hour-fold/shard ingestion, configuration/tombstone loads, policy compatibility, model acceptance, full long-window measurement and native capacity remain separate work.
 
 New canonical raw/hourly publications store a leading reserved `_summary` version1 in the same JSON object and the same single put as all original report fields. The summary's first line ends with comma+LF and is limited to64KiB UTF-8 including framing; the complete canonical object remains limited to8MiB. Explicit custom/empty/preset arrays remain response-only and do not acquire this storage-summary limit. Public POST/day GET report shapes remain unchanged. Window reads request the first64KiB and validate only the summary, preserving raw arm counts and normalized coverage without parsing grids. All received bytes, including chunk tails, count toward the window budget. This does not verify unread grid/tail integrity. Legacy objects use a verified complete small read or a separate bounded full read as the sole version, charging prefix plus fallback bytes; a disappeared or corrupt fallback is unavailable, not missing. Older writers can restore the coherent but slower legacy format. There is no sidecar, dual-write consistency protocol, migration or history repair. Local range/byte evidence is not deployed Worker capacity, policy compatibility or scientific/customer acceptance.
